cards.key: A stone thrown at 10 m/s from a 44.1 m cliff falls for 3 s and lands 30 m away. At impact vy = g·t, and the speed is v = √(10² + 29.4²) ≈ 31 m/s.

cards.h: Launch at an angle: split the velocity in two
cards.p: For a launch at an angle, the velocity splits into two components. The horizontal component v<sub>x</sub> = v<sub>0</sub>·cosθ does not change. The vertical component v<sub>0y</sub> = v<sub>0</sub>·sinθ drops by 9.8 m/s each second.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='20' y1='170' x2='300' y2='170' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><line x1='60' y1='170' x2='137' y2='170' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='3' fill='none'/><polygon points='144,170 134,174.5 134,165.5' fill='var(--c1)'/><line x1='144' y1='170' x2='144' y2='65' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='3' fill='none'/><polygon points='144,58 148.5,68 139.5,68' fill='var(--c2)'/><line x1='60' y1='170' x2='139.8' y2='63.6' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='3' fill='none'/><polygon points='144,58 141.6,68.7 134.4,63.3' fill='var(--acc)'/><path d='M85 170 A25 25 0 0 0 75 150' fill='none' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='88' y='163' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>53°</text><text x='88' y='95' font-size='12' fill='var(--acc)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>v₀ = 20 m/s</text><text x='102' y='188' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle'>vx = 12 m/s</text><text x='152' y='110' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)'>vy = 16 m/s</text><rect x='200' y='30' width='110' height='60' fill='var(--panel)' rx='8'/><text x='255' y='55' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>cos53° = 0.6</text><text x='255' y='77' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>sin53° = 0.8</text><text x='200' y='140' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)'>vx: always the same</text><text x='200' y='160' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)'>vy: drops with g</text></svg>
cards.key: The horizontal velocity vx = v0·cosθ stays constant, and the vertical velocity changes as vy = v0·sinθ − g·t. For 20 m/s at 53°, vx = 12 m/s and v0y = 16 m/s.

once.soru: Which component of the velocity of a ball launched at an angle stays the same during the flight?

secenekler.neden: There is no horizontal force. So vx stays constant.
Gravity lowers the vertical velocity by 9.8 m/s each second.
Gravity only acts in the vertical direction.

cards.h: The top of the path and the time of flight
cards.p: At the top v<sub>y</sub> = 0, and the time to get there is v<sub>0y</sub> / g. For an object that lands at its launch level, the way down takes as long as the way up. So the total time is T = 2·v<sub>0y</sub> / g.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='40' y1='100' x2='306.4' y2='100' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='312,100 304,103.6 304,96.4' fill='var(--ink)'/><line x1='40' y1='185' x2='40' y2='15' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><line x1='40' y1='60' x2='287.4' y2='60' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><line x1='40' y1='30.7' x2='287.4' y2='169.3' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><circle cx='163.7' cy='100' r='4' fill='var(--ink)'/><line x1='287.4' y1='95' x2='287.4' y2='105' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><text x='45' y='14' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)'>velocity (m/s)</text><text x='175' y='52' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)'>vx = 10 m/s (constant)</text><text x='70' y='30' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' font-weight='bold'>vy</text><text x='35' y='34' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>17.3</text><text x='155' y='118' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>top: vy = 0</text><text x='287' y='92' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>T ≈ 3.5 s</text><text x='283' y='190' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>−17.3</text><text x='300' y='118' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)'>t</text></svg>
cards.key: The maximum height is v0y² / (2g). The total time is T = 2·v0·sinθ / g. If v0y ≈ 17.3 m/s, then T ≈ 3.5 s.

cards.p: The total horizontal distance covered is called the range: R = v0²·sin2θ / g. For an object that lands at its launch level, the longest range comes at 45°. 30° and 60° give the same range.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='20' y1='180' x2='305' y2='180' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><path d='M40 180 Q146 -3.6 252 180' fill='none' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M40 180 Q162.5 57.6 285 180' fill='none' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2.5'/><path d='M40 180 Q146 118.8 252 180' fill='none' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2'/><text x='146' y='80' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>60°</text><text x='162.5' y='113' font-size='12' fill='var(--c3)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>45°</text><text x='146' y='143' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>30°</text><line x1='252' y1='175' x2='252' y2='185' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><line x1='285' y1='175' x2='285' y2='185' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><text x='246' y='197' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>35.3</text><text x='292' y='197' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>40.8 m</text><text x='10' y='20' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>v₀ = 20 m/s (all)</text><text x='10' y='38' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)'>g ≈ 9.8 m/s²</text></svg>
cards.key: The range is R = v0²·sin2θ / g, and it is largest at θ = 45°.

etk.soru: Change the speed and the angle. Compare 30° with 60°. Which angle gives the longest range?

cards.h: Launch at an angle from a height
cards.p: For an object that lands lower than where it started, the formulas for T and range do not apply. Take up as positive and solve −h = v<sub>0y</sub>·t − ½·g·t².
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='310' y='20' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='end'>v<tspan font-size='9' baseline-shift='sub'>x</tspan> = 10 m/s, v<tspan font-size='9' baseline-shift='sub'>0y</tspan> = 14.7 m/s</text><text x='310' y='38' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='end'>g = 9.8 m/s²</text><rect x='20' y='80' width='40' height='100' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='10' y1='180' x2='310' y2='180' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M60 80 Q160 -70 260 180' fill='none' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><line x1='60' y1='80' x2='74.1' y2='58.8' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='78,53 76.2,63.8 68.7,58.8' fill='var(--acc)'/><text x='84' y='58' font-size='12' fill='var(--acc)' font-weight='bold'>v₀</text><circle cx='60' cy='80' r='4' fill='var(--c2)'/><circle cx='260' cy='180' r='4' fill='var(--c2)'/><text x='40' y='134' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>19.6 m</text><path d='M60 80 H300' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-dasharray='3 3'/><text x='300' y='74' font-size='10' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='end'>launch level</text><text x='230' y='165' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>t = 4 s</text><text x='160' y='196' font-size='11' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>−19.6 = 14.7t − 4.9t² → t = 4 s, x = 40 m</text></svg>
cards.key: For an object launched from a height of 19.6 m with v0y = 14.7 m/s and vx = 10 m/s, t = 4 s and x = 40 m.

once.soru: Two stones are thrown with the same speed and angle, one from level ground and the other from a high cliff. Which one stays in the air longer?

secenekler.neden: After coming back to its launch level, it falls further by the height of the cliff.
The stone thrown from the cliff passes its launch level and keeps falling. So its time is longer.
The extra fall down the cliff adds time.

cards.p: An object thrown from a moving vehicle also carries the vehicle's velocity. A ball thrown straight up from a truck moving at constant velocity comes straight back down for someone on the truck. For someone on the ground, it follows a projectile path.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='160' y='20' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>the truck moves at a constant 10 m/s</text><line x1='10' y1='170' x2='310' y2='170' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><g opacity='1'><rect x='30' y='130' width='60' height='30' rx='3' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='45' cy='163' r='7' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='80' cy='163' r='7' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/></g><g opacity='0.55'><rect x='210' y='130' width='60' height='30' rx='3' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='225' cy='163' r='7' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='260' cy='163' r='7' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/></g><path d='M60 130 Q150 -50 240 130' fill='none' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><line x1='60' y1='128' x2='60' y2='69' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='2' fill='none'/><polygon points='60,62 64.5,72 55.5,72' fill='var(--c5)'/><circle cx='60' cy='130' r='5' fill='var(--c2)'/><circle cx='240' cy='130' r='5' fill='var(--c2)'/><line x1='96' y1='145' x2='127' y2='145' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='134,145 124,149.5 124,140.5' fill='var(--c3)'/><text x='115' y='136' font-size='11' fill='var(--c3)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>10 m/s</text><text x='20' y='192' font-size='11' fill='var(--c5)' font-weight='bold'>truck view: straight up</text><text x='310' y='192' font-size='11' fill='var(--acc)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>ground view: a curve</text></svg>
cards.key: The object's initial velocity relative to the ground is its launch velocity relative to the vehicle plus the vehicle's velocity.

once.soru: A ball is thrown straight up from the bed of a truck moving at constant velocity. With no air resistance, where does the ball land?

secenekler.neden: The ball carries the truck's horizontal velocity. So it moves along with the truck horizontally.
The ball does not lose its horizontal velocity. It keeps the same horizontal velocity as the truck.
The ball's horizontal velocity is not greater than the truck's.

cards.p: The formulas ignore air resistance. In reality, air slows the ball, the range and height get smaller, and the descent is steeper. The angle for the longest range is usually less than 45°.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='15' y1='180' x2='305' y2='180' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><path d='M30 180 Q150 60 270 180' fill='none' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><path d='M30 180 C90 120 165 100 200 180' fill='none' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2.5'/><text x='222' y='112' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' font-weight='bold'>no air</text><text x='110' y='170' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' font-weight='bold'>in air</text><text x='160' y='30' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>range and height get smaller</text><line x1='200' y1='175' x2='200' y2='185' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><line x1='270' y1='175' x2='270' y2='185' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><text x='200' y='197' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' text-anchor='middle'>short</text><text x='270' y='197' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle'>long</text></svg>
cards.key: Without air, the path is a symmetric parabola. In air, the path is shorter and not symmetric.

once.soru: In a real game, how does the ball's range compare with what the no-air formula gives?

secenekler.neden: Air slows the ball. So the ball covers a shorter distance.
Air does not give the ball energy. It slows it down.
The formula ignores air, but in reality there is a difference.

cards.p:
• Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.
• Horizontally vx is constant, and vertically the acceleration is g.
• At the top vy = 0, and T = 2·v0·sinθ / g.
• The range is R = v0²·sin2θ / g, and it is largest at 45°.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 210' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='15' y1='170' x2='305' y2='170' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><path d='M30 170 Q160 10 290 170' fill='none' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2.5'/><line x1='30' y1='170' x2='55.8' y2='135.6' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='60,130 57.6,140.7 50.4,135.3' fill='var(--acc)'/><line x1='160' y1='90' x2='188' y2='90' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='195,90 185,94.5 185,85.5' fill='var(--acc)'/><text x='160' y='75' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>top: vy = 0</text><line x1='34.9' y1='185' x2='285.1' y2='185' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='290,185 283,188.2 283,181.8' fill='var(--muted)'/><polygon points='30,185 37,181.8 37,188.2' fill='var(--muted)'/><text x='160' y='204' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>range R</text><text x='10' y='20' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)'>horizontal: constant velocity</text><text x='10' y='38' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)'>vertical: free fall</text></svg>

quiz.q: A stone is thrown horizontally at 15 m/s from a cliff 78.4 m high. How many meters from the base of the cliff does it land? (g = 9.8 m/s², no air resistance)
quiz.e: Vertically h = ½·g·t²: 78.4 = 4.9·t², t² = 16, and t = 4 s. Horizontally x = v<sub>0</sub>·t = 15·4 = 60 m.

quiz.q: While a ball launched at an angle is in flight (no air resistance), which quantities change and which stay constant?
quiz.e: There is no horizontal force, so v<sub>x</sub> is constant, and the acceleration is g at every moment. v<sub>y</sub> changes by g each second. That is why the height and the speed also change, and the speed is smallest at the top.

quiz.q: A ball is launched from the ground at speed v<sub>0</sub> and angle θ and lands at the same level. Match each quantity with its formula.
quiz.e: At the top v<sub>y</sub> = 0, so the time to the top is v<sub>0y</sub> / g and the height is v<sub>0y</sub>² / (2g). The way down takes as long as the way up, so T = 2·v<sub>0y</sub> / g. The range is R = v<sub>0</sub>²·sin2θ / g.

quiz.q: A ball is launched from the ground at 19.6 m/s, at 30° above the horizontal. What is the maximum height it reaches, in meters? (g = 9.8 m/s², sin30° = 0.5)
quiz.e: v<sub>0y</sub> = 19.6·0.5 = 9.8 m/s. At the top v<sub>y</sub> = 0, so h = v<sub>0y</sub>² / (2g) = 96.04 / 19.6 = 4.9 m.

cembersel-hareket.title: Circular and rotational motion
cembersel-hareket.summary: Learn why a turning object is accelerating. Explore curves, vertical circles, and angular momentum.

cards.p: If an object on a circle covers equal distances in equal times, it is in uniform circular motion. Its speed is constant, but its velocity is always tangent and keeps changing direction. So the object is accelerating.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><circle cx='100' cy='100' r='65' fill='none' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='100' r='3' fill='var(--ink)'/><line x1='100' y1='100' x2='165' y2='100' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><text x='128' y='94' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)'>r</text><line x1='100' y1='35' x2='64' y2='35' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2.5'/><polygon points='55,35 64,30.9 64,39' fill='var(--c1)'/><line x1='35' y1='100' x2='35' y2='136' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2.5'/><polygon points='35,145 30.9,136 39,136' fill='var(--c1)'/><line x1='100' y1='165' x2='136' y2='165' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2.5'/><polygon points='145,165 136,169.1 136,160.9' fill='var(--c1)'/><line x1='165' y1='100' x2='165' y2='64' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2.5'/><polygon points='165,55 169.1,64 160.9,64' fill='var(--c1)'/><circle cx='100' cy='35' r='6' fill='var(--c1)'/><circle cx='35' cy='100' r='6' fill='var(--c1)'/><circle cx='100' cy='165' r='6' fill='var(--c1)'/><circle cx='165' cy='100' r='6' fill='var(--c1)'/><text x='76' y='26' font-size='13' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>v</text><text x='26' y='127' font-size='13' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>v</text><text x='124' y='186' font-size='13' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>v</text><text x='174' y='80' font-size='13' fill='var(--c1)' font-weight='bold'>v</text><text x='205' y='60' font-size='13' fill='var(--c3)' font-weight='bold'>speed: constant</text><text x='205' y='92' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>direction of velocity:</text><text x='205' y='110' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>keeps changing</text><text x='205' y='145' font-size='13' fill='var(--acc)' font-weight='bold'>→ it accelerates</text></svg>
cards.key: The speed is constant, but the velocity vector changes. That is why uniform circular motion is accelerated motion.

cards.p: The time for one turn is the period (T). The number of turns per second is the frequency (f). f = 1/T, and frequency is measured in hertz (1/s).
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><circle cx='80' cy='100' r='50' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='80' cy='50' r='6' fill='var(--c1)'/><path d='M80 38 A62 62 0 1 0 137.5 76.8' fill='none' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='137.5' y1='76.8' x2='136.8' y2='75.3' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='132.7,67.3 140.4,73.5 133.1,77.2' fill='var(--acc)'/><text x='80' y='98' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>1 turn</text><text x='80' y='116' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>time: T</text><text x='80' y='188' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>T: the time for one turn</text><rect x='165' y='28' width='148' height='145' rx='8' fill='var(--panel)'/><text x='239' y='52' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>1200 turns per minute</text><text x='239' y='78' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>f = 1200 / 60 s</text><text x='239' y='102' font-size='14' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>f = 20 Hz</text><text x='239' y='132' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>T = 1 / f</text><text x='239' y='156' font-size='14' fill='var(--c2)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>T = 0.05 s</text></svg>
cards.key: For a drum spinning at 1200 turns per minute, f = 20 Hz and T = 0.05 s. The longer the period, the lower the frequency.

cards.p: In one turn the object travels 2πr, so v = 2πr/T. The angular speed is ω = 2π/T (rad/s). The two are linked by v = ω·r.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><circle cx='95' cy='105' r='75' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='95' y1='105' x2='170' y2='105' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><circle cx='95' cy='105' r='3' fill='var(--ink)'/><path d='M95 85 A20 20 0 0 0 76.2 98.2' fill='none' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='76.2' y1='98.2' x2='76.2' y2='98.5' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='75.5,106.5 72.6,98.2 79.8,98.8' fill='var(--c5)'/><text x='70' y='86' font-size='13' fill='var(--c5)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>ω</text><line x1='132' y1='105' x2='132' y2='84' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2.5'/><polygon points='132,75 136.1,84 128,84' fill='var(--c1)'/><line x1='170' y1='105' x2='170' y2='54' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2.5'/><polygon points='170,45 174.1,54 165.9,54' fill='var(--c1)'/><circle cx='132' cy='105' r='4' fill='var(--ink)'/><circle cx='170' cy='105' r='4' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='132' y='124' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>A</text><text x='178' y='124' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>B</text><text x='126' y='88' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='end'>vA</text><text x='178' y='70' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)'>vB</text><text x='205' y='40' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>v = 2πr/T</text><text x='205' y='62' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>ω = 2π/T</text><text x='205' y='92' font-size='15' fill='var(--c1)' font-weight='bold'>v = ω·r</text><text x='205' y='130' font-size='12' fill='var(--c5)'>ω: the same for all</text><text x='205' y='152' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>rB = 2·rA</text><text x='205' y='174' font-size='13' fill='var(--c1)' font-weight='bold'>vB = 2·vA</text></svg>
cards.key: On a Ferris wheel every point has the same angular speed, but the linear speed grows with the radius. One turn equals 2π rad, or 360°.

cards.p: The acceleration that changes the direction of the velocity always points toward the center, and a = v²/r = ω²·r. It is perpendicular to the velocity, so it changes only the direction, not the speed.

once.soru: If you take the same curve twice as fast, how many times larger is the centripetal acceleration?

secenekler.neden: Since a = v²/r, the acceleration grows with the square of the speed: 2² = 4 times.
The acceleration grows with the square of the speed, not with the speed.
The radius stayed the same, but the speed went up. The acceleration depends on the speed.

cards.h: Centripetal force is not a new force
cards.p: Centripetal acceleration needs a net force toward the center, and that force is F = m·v²/r. Forces you already know supply it: tension, friction, or gravity.

cards.h: A car on a curve: friction
cards.p: On a level road, the force that turns a car through a curve is static friction. So the maximum safe speed is v = √(μs·g·r), and it does not depend on mass.

etk.soru: Change the road's coefficient of friction and the radius of the curve. Dry asphalt μ ≈ 0.7, wet ≈ 0.4, ice ≈ 0.1.

cards.p: On a banked curve, the horizontal component of the normal force points toward the center. So even without friction you can turn safely at one particular speed. That speed comes from tanθ = v²/(r·g).

once.soru: Why are the curves on racetracks tilted inward?

secenekler.yazi: So the road pushes the car toward the center
secenekler.neden: The normal force of a tilted road points partly toward the center. So friction has less work to do.
The tilt does drain water, but the main purpose is to make turning easier.
The opposite. The tilt lets cars take the curve faster.

cards.p: When an object on a string moves in a horizontal circle, the string makes an angle α with the vertical. The vertical component of the tension balances the weight, and the horizontal component supplies the centripetal force. So tanα = v²/(r·g).
cards.key: T·cosα = m·g and T·sinα = m·v²/r. The faster the object, the closer the string gets to horizontal.

once.soru: You tie a stone to a string and whirl it horizontally above your head. Can the string be exactly horizontal?

secenekler.neden: Balancing the weight takes an upward component of the tension. So the string always slopes down a little.

secenekler.yazi: Yes, if you whirl it fast
secenekler.neden: The faster it goes, the closer the string gets to horizontal. But because of the weight, it never gets exactly there.
When you whirl it slowly, the string clearly hangs downward.

cards.h: Vertical circle: minimum speed at the top
cards.p: At the top of a vertical circle, the weight and the tension both point toward the center, so W + T = m·v²/r. At the limit T = 0, this gives v = √(g·r). If the object is slower than that, the string goes slack.

once.soru: You whirl a stone on a string in a vertical circle. Where is the string pulled tightest?

secenekler.neden: At the bottom, the tension has to both overcome the weight and supply the centripetal force.
At the top, the weight does part of the job. So the tension is smallest there.
The weight always points down. So the tension changes with position.

cards.p: When a car turns, you feel pushed against the door. In fact your body keeps going straight because of inertia, and the door pushes you toward the center. No real force pushes you outward.

cards.key: “Centrifugal” is only an inertia effect felt by the turning observer. For an observer on the ground, there is only a net force toward the center.

once.soru: When a car turns left, what presses you against the door on the right?

secenekler.neden: Your body wants to go straight. The car turns underneath you, and the door pushes you toward the center.
No real force pushes you outward. It is only a feeling.
Friction from the seat tries to turn you with the car. It does not push you outward.

cards.p: The measure of resistance to rotation is called the moment of inertia: I = Σm·r². The farther the mass is spread from the axis, the larger I is. For a ring I = M·R², and for a solid disk it is ½·M·R².

cards.key: I depends not only on the mass but also on how far the mass is from the axis of rotation.

once.soru: A ring and a solid disk have the same mass and radius. Which one is harder to start spinning?

secenekler.neden: All of the ring's mass is far from the axis. So it resists rotation more.
Part of the disk's mass is close to the axis. So it resists less.
The mass is the same, but it is spread differently. Resistance to rotation depends on how the mass is spread.

cards.p: The angular momentum of a rotating object is L = I·ω. With no external torque, angular momentum is conserved, so I1·ω1 = I2·ω2. For a point object, L = m·r·v⊥.

cards.p: The kinetic energy of a rotating object is ½·I·ω². When an object rolls without slipping, its energy is shared between moving forward and rotating. So it comes down more slowly than a box sliding without friction.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><text x='160' y='22' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>bottom speed from the same height h (× √(g·h))</text><line x1='110' y1='38' x2='110' y2='170' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><rect x='110' y='45' width='169.7' height='20' rx='3' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.45' stroke='var(--c3)'/><text x='103' y='59' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>sliding box</text><text x='285.7' y='59' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>1.41</text><rect x='110' y='77' width='143.4' height='20' rx='3' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.45' stroke='var(--c1)'/><text x='103' y='91' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>solid sphere</text><text x='259.4' y='91' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>1.20</text><rect x='110' y='109' width='138.6' height='20' rx='3' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.45' stroke='var(--c4)'/><text x='103' y='123' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>solid cylinder</text><text x='254.6' y='123' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>1.15</text><rect x='110' y='141' width='120' height='20' rx='3' fill='var(--c2)' fill-opacity='0.45' stroke='var(--c2)'/><text x='103' y='155' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>thin ring</text><text x='236' y='155' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>1.00</text><text x='160' y='192' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>the box slides without friction, the others roll without slipping</text></svg>
cards.key: In rolling, v = ω·r and the total energy is ½·m·v² + ½·I·ω².

once.soru: A solid cylinder and a thin ring roll down the same ramp at the same moment. Which one gets down first?

secenekler.neden: The cylinder has a smaller I. Less of its energy goes into rotation, so it moves forward faster.
The ring has a large I. Most of its energy goes into rotation, so it moves forward slowly.
Their mass is spread differently. So they share the energy differently.

cards.p:
• The speed is constant, the direction of the velocity changes, and f = 1/T.
• Linear speed is v = ω·r = 2πr/T.
• F = m·v²/r is not a new force. It is the net force toward the center.
• On a curve v ≤ √(μ·g·r), and at the top of a vertical circle v ≥ √(g·r).
• With no external torque, L = I·ω is conserved.

quiz.q: With arms out, a skater has a moment of inertia of 3 kg·m² and spins at 2 turns per second. Pulling the arms in lowers the moment of inertia to 1.2 kg·m². How many turns per second does the skater make now? (no external torque)
quiz.e: Angular momentum is conserved, so I<sub>1</sub>·f<sub>1</sub> = I<sub>2</sub>·f<sub>2</sub>. Since 3·2 = 1.2·f<sub>2</sub>, f<sub>2</sub> = 5 turns/s.

quiz.q: For an object in uniform circular motion, put each quantity in the right group.
quiz.e: Since the speed is constant, so are the period, ω, and ½·m·v². The velocity is always tangent, and the acceleration and net force always point toward the center, so the direction of these three changes at every moment.

quiz.q: Which force supplies the centripetal force in each case? Match them.
ciftler: A stone whirled on a string
A car turning on a level curve
A car on a frictionless banked curve
Horizontal component of the normal force
quiz.e: Centripetal force is not a new force. For the stone it is the string tension, on a level curve it is static friction, and for the Moon it is gravity. On a banked curve it is the horizontal component of the normal force, which points toward the center.

quiz.q: A vertical loop at an amusement park has a radius of 10 m. What minimum speed, in m/s, does the car need at the top to keep pressing on the track? (g = 10 m/s²)
quiz.e: At the top, in the limiting case, the weight alone supplies the centripetal force, so m·g = m·v²/r. That gives v = √(g·r) = √(10·10) = 10 m/s.

kutle-cekimi.title: Gravitation
kutle-cekimi.summary: Newton's law of gravitation, g, Kepler's laws, and satellites.

cards.p: Every object with mass attracts other objects, and the force is F = G·m1·m2/r2. Here r is the distance between the centers of the two objects. G is a very small number.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><defs><marker id='kcek-1' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c2)'/></marker><marker id='kcek-2' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--muted)'/></marker></defs><text x='160' y='34' font-size='20' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>F = G · m₁ · m₂ / r²</text><circle cx='70' cy='95' r='24' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='250' cy='95' r='15' fill='var(--c5)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='70' y='100' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>m₁</text><text x='250' y='100' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>m₂</text><line x1='97' y1='95' x2='140' y2='95' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='3' marker-end='url(#kcek-1)'/><line x1='232' y1='95' x2='190' y2='95' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='3' marker-end='url(#kcek-1)'/><text x='118' y='84' font-size='13' fill='var(--c2)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>F</text><text x='212' y='84' font-size='13' fill='var(--c2)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>F</text><line x1='70' y1='135' x2='70' y2='150' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='250' y1='135' x2='250' y2='150' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='73' y1='142' x2='247' y2='142' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.2' marker-start='url(#kcek-2)' marker-end='url(#kcek-2)'/><text x='160' y='162' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>r: distance from center to center</text><text x='160' y='188' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>G ≈ 6.67×10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²</text></svg>
cards.key: G is about 6.67×10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². r is the distance between the centers, not between the surfaces.

once.soru: Does the friend sitting next to you attract you?

secenekler.neden: Every object with mass attracts. G is so small that you cannot feel this force.
Gravity is not only for planets. Every mass attracts.
Gravity acts at a distance. No contact is needed.

cards.p: The force is proportional to the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance. If the distance doubles, the force drops to 1/4. If it triples, the force drops to 1/9.
cards.key: If one of the masses doubles, the force doubles. If the distance is cut in half, the force becomes 4 times larger.

cards.p: Two objects attract each other with forces of the same magnitude in opposite directions. The accelerations come from a = F/m. An apple falls at 9.8 m/s², while Earth's acceleration is about 10−25 m/s².
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><defs><marker id='kcek-3' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c2)'/></marker><marker id='kcek-4' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c1)'/></marker></defs><text x='160' y='22' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>equal magnitude, opposite direction, different objects</text><circle cx='85' cy='100' r='55' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.2' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='85' y='140' font-size='13' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Earth</text><circle cx='260' cy='100' r='10' fill='var(--c2)' fill-opacity='0.4' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='260' y='128' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>apple</text><line x1='248' y1='100' x2='200' y2='100' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='3' marker-end='url(#kcek-3)'/><text x='224' y='90' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>≈ 1 N</text><line x1='85' y1='100' x2='133' y2='100' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='3' marker-end='url(#kcek-4)'/><text x='103' y='90' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>≈ 1 N</text><text x='85' y='182' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>a ≈ 2×10⁻²⁵ m/s²</text><text x='250' y='182' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>a ≈ 9.8 m/s²</text></svg>
cards.key: This is Newton's third law. The forces are equal, but the accelerations are not. The object with less mass accelerates more.

cards.p: Every mass creates a gravitational field around it, and g = F/m. That gives g = G·M/r2. g does not depend on the mass of the falling object, and at the surface it is about 9.8 m/s².
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><defs><marker id='kcek-5' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c3)'/></marker></defs><circle cx='85' cy='100' r='32' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.25' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='85' y='105' font-size='14' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>M</text><line x1='157.063' y1='129.849' x2='121.955' y2='115.307' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-5)'/><line x1='114.849' y1='172.063' x2='100.307' y2='136.955' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-5)'/><line x1='55.1507' y1='172.063' x2='69.6927' y2='136.955' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-5)'/><line x1='12.9374' y1='129.849' x2='48.0448' y2='115.307' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-5)'/><line x1='12.9374' y1='70.1507' x2='48.0448' y2='84.6927' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-5)'/><line x1='55.1507' y1='27.9374' x2='69.6927' y2='63.0448' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-5)'/><line x1='114.849' y1='27.9374' x2='100.307' y2='63.0448' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-5)'/><line x1='157.063' y1='70.1507' x2='121.955' y2='84.6927' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-5)'/><text x='185' y='55' font-size='18' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='700'>g = G·M / r²</text><text x='185' y='85' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)'>g = F / m</text><text x='185' y='105' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)'>unit: N/kg = m/s²</text><text x='185' y='135' font-size='13' fill='var(--c3)' font-weight='700'>surface: ≈ 9.8 m/s²</text><text x='185' y='160' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)'>M: mass of the planet</text><text x='185' y='178' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)'>r: distance to center</text></svg>
cards.key: The gravitational field is the gravitational force per unit mass. g depends only on the planet's mass (M) and the distance from its center (r).

once.soru: If a planet kept the same mass but had half the radius, what would g at its surface be?

secenekler.neden: Since g = GM/r², halving r makes r² one quarter as large, so g becomes 4 times larger.
g is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, not to the distance.
The mass is the same, but the surface is closer to the center. g depends on distance.

cards.h: g is not the same everywhere
cards.p: g gets smaller as you move away from the center, and on the Moon g is about 1.6 m/s². Your mass (kg) is the same everywhere. Your weight (N) equals m·g, so it changes from place to place.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><text x='200' y='18' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>g (m/s²)</text><text x='12' y='47' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>Earth's surface</text><rect x='125' y='33' width='137.2' height='18' rx='3' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1'/><text x='268.2' y='47' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='700'>9.8</text><text x='12' y='77' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>400 km (ISS)</text><rect x='125' y='63' width='121.8' height='18' rx='3' fill='var(--c5)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1'/><text x='252.8' y='77' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='700'>≈ 8.7</text><text x='12' y='107' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>h = R (r = 2R)</text><rect x='125' y='93' width='34.3' height='18' rx='3' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1'/><text x='165.3' y='107' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='700'>≈ 2.45</text><text x='12' y='137' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>Moon's surface</text><rect x='125' y='123' width='22.68' height='18' rx='3' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1'/><text x='153.68' y='137' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='700'>≈ 1.6</text><line x1='10' y1='160' x2='310' y2='160' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-width='1'/><text x='160' y='180' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>m = 50 kg: weight 490 N on Earth, ≈ 80 N on the Moon</text></svg>
cards.key: If you rise a height R above the ground, r = 2R and g drops to one quarter (≈ 2.45 m/s²).

etk.soru: Rise above the ground. How do g and your weight change? (Earth's radius ≈ 6370 km)

cards.p: Planets move around the Sun in elliptical orbits, with the Sun at one focus of the ellipse. The point closest to the Sun is the perihelion, and the farthest point is the aphelion.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><ellipse cx='160' cy='105' rx='110' ry='75' fill='none' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='79.5326' cy='105' r='9' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.8' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='94.5326' y='109' font-size='12' fill='var(--c4)' font-weight='700'>Sun (focus)</text><line x1='236.467' y1='101' x2='244.467' y2='109' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='236.467' y1='109' x2='244.467' y2='101' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='240.467' y='93' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>empty focus</text><circle cx='215' cy='40.0481' r='6' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.9' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1'/><text x='225' y='28.0481' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' font-weight='700'>planet</text><text x='46' y='109' font-size='11' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>closest</text><text x='274' y='109' font-size='11' fill='var(--ink)'>farthest</text><text x='12' y='20' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='700'>1st law: the orbit is an ellipse</text><text x='160' y='193' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>real orbits are very close to circles (drawing exaggerated)</text></svg>
cards.key: The Sun is at one focus of the ellipse, not at its center. Earth's orbit is almost a circle.

once.soru: What is the shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun?

secenekler.neden: Earth's orbit is an ellipse that is very close to a circle, with the Sun at one focus.
The orbit is close to a circle, but not exactly one. The distance changes a little over the year.
The orbit is closed, and Earth does not fall into the Sun.

cards.p: Kepler's second law explains why a planet speeds up at perihelion. It says the line joining the Sun and the planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times. The seasons, though, come from the tilt of the axis, not from the distance.
cards.key: This law comes from the conservation of angular momentum (L = m·r·v⊥). Earth reaches perihelion in early January, when it is winter in the northern hemisphere.

cards.p: The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the average distance, so T²/r³ = constant. The constant depends on the mass at the center. A distant planet has a longer year.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><text x='160' y='32' font-size='18' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>T² / r³ = constant</text><rect x='15' y='48' width='290' height='26' rx='4' fill='var(--panel)'/><text x='55' y='66' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>planet</text><text x='135' y='66' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>r (AU)</text><text x='205' y='66' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>T (years)</text><text x='272' y='66' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>T²/r³</text><text x='55' y='96' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>Earth</text><text x='135' y='96' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>1</text><text x='205' y='96' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>1</text><text x='272' y='96' font-size='12' fill='var(--c3)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>1</text><text x='55' y='120' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>Mars</text><text x='135' y='120' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>1.52</text><text x='205' y='120' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>1.88</text><text x='272' y='120' font-size='12' fill='var(--c3)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>≈ 1</text><text x='55' y='144' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>Jupiter</text><text x='135' y='144' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>5.20</text><text x='205' y='144' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>11.9</text><text x='272' y='144' font-size='12' fill='var(--c3)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>≈ 1</text><line x1='15' y1='160' x2='305' y2='160' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-width='1'/><text x='160' y='184' font-size='13' fill='var(--acc)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>r × 4 → T² × 64 → T × 8</text></svg>
cards.key: r is the semi-major axis of the ellipse. The constant is the same only for objects orbiting the same central body.

etk.soru: The farther from the Sun, the longer the year. Put the planets in order of orbital period, from shortest to longest.

once.soru: A planet is 4 times farther from the Sun than Earth. How many Earth years long is its year?

secenekler.neden: Since T² ∝ r³, 4³ = 64 and √64 = 8.
The period is not directly proportional to the distance.
16 is 4². But it is the cube of the distance that is proportional to the square of the period.

cards.h: A satellite: an object that is always falling
cards.p: The force that keeps a satellite in orbit is gravity. From G·M·m/r² = m·v²/r we get v = √(G·M/r). The satellite's mass cancels, and the lower the orbit, the higher the speed.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><defs><marker id='kcek-8' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c3)'/></marker><marker id='kcek-9' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c2)'/></marker></defs><circle cx='85' cy='100' r='30' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.25' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='85' y='105' font-size='13' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>M</text><circle cx='85' cy='100' r='70' fill='none' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><circle cx='85' cy='30' r='6' fill='var(--c5)' fill-opacity='0.9' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='93' y1='30' x2='143' y2='30' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2.5' marker-end='url(#kcek-8)'/><text x='147' y='26' font-size='13' fill='var(--c3)' font-weight='700'>v</text><line x1='85' y1='38' x2='85' y2='65' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2.5' marker-end='url(#kcek-9)'/><text x='91' y='56' font-size='13' fill='var(--c2)' font-weight='700'>F</text><text x='175' y='58' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>gravity = centripetal</text><text x='175' y='88' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)'>G·M·m/r² = m·v²/r</text><text x='175' y='130' font-size='18' fill='var(--acc)' font-weight='700'>v = √(G·M/r)</text><text x='175' y='160' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' font-weight='700'>m cancels</text><text x='160' y='192' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>orbital speed does not depend on the satellite's mass</text></svg>
cards.key: Gravity acts as the centripetal force (see Circular and rotational motion). A heavy satellite and a light one in the same orbit move at the same speed.

cards.p: A satellite whose period equals Earth's rotation period (24 hours) is called geosynchronous. If it orbits above the equator, it is called geostationary. At a height of about 36 000 km, it always stays above the same point.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><defs><marker id='kcek-10' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c1)'/></marker><marker id='kcek-11' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c5)'/></marker></defs><text x='12' y='20' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)'>view from above the North Pole (not to scale)</text><circle cx='85' cy='105' r='64' fill='none' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><circle cx='85' cy='105' r='26' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.25' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M 99 93 A 18 18 0 1 0 100 115' fill='none' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5' marker-end='url(#kcek-10)'/><line x1='111' y1='105' x2='143' y2='105' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='2 2'/><circle cx='111' cy='105' r='3' fill='var(--c2)' fill-opacity='1' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='1'/><circle cx='149' cy='105' r='6' fill='var(--c5)' fill-opacity='0.9' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='149' y1='113' x2='149' y2='71' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#kcek-11)'/><text x='165' y='58' font-size='14' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='700'>T ≈ 24 hours</text><text x='165' y='85' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>in the equatorial plane</text><text x='165' y='107' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>same direction as Earth</text><text x='165' y='129' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>≈ 36 000 km altitude</text><text x='165' y='160' font-size='12' fill='var(--c5)' font-weight='700'>looks fixed</text><text x='165' y='178' font-size='12' fill='var(--c5)' font-weight='700'>in the sky</text></svg>
cards.key: A geostationary satellite moves in a circular orbit in the same direction as Earth's rotation. TV and communication satellites work this way. A circular orbit with a 24-hour period has only one possible radius.

once.soru: Why does a satellite dish on a roof always point the same way without ever being turned?

secenekler.neden: The satellite goes around once every 24 hours. It turns at the same rate as Earth, so it looks fixed in the sky.
If the satellite stood still, it would fall to Earth. It actually moves at about 3 km per second.

secenekler.yazi: The signal comes from every direction
secenekler.neden: The signal comes from one satellite, and the dish has to face it.

cards.p: On the space station (about 400 km up), g is still about 8.7 m/s², so gravity is there. The station and the astronaut are in free fall together. That is why a scale reads 0.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><defs><marker id='kcek-12' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c3)'/></marker><marker id='kcek-13' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c2)'/></marker></defs><circle cx='160' cy='480' r='300' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.15' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='160' cy='480' r='355' fill='none' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><rect x='144' y='118' width='32' height='14' rx='3' fill='var(--c5)' fill-opacity='0.4' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='176' y1='125' x2='236' y2='125' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2.5' marker-end='url(#kcek-12)'/><text x='242' y='129' font-size='12' fill='var(--c3)' font-weight='700'>v ≈ 7.7 km/s</text><line x1='160' y1='134' x2='160' y2='168' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2.5' marker-end='url(#kcek-13)'/><text x='168' y='160' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' font-weight='700'>g ≈ 8.7 m/s²</text><text x='160' y='22' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>at ≈ 400 km, gravity is not gone</text><text x='160' y='48' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>the station and the astronaut fall freely together</text><text x='160' y='70' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>the scale reads 0 → feeling of weightlessness</text><text x='160' y='108' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>station</text><text x='160' y='196' font-size='11' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Earth</text></svg>
cards.key: Thanks to their sideways speed, the station and the astronaut keep missing Earth. Weightlessness is free fall, not the absence of gravity.

cards.p: The minimum speed needed to break free of a planet's gravity and never come back is the escape velocity: v = √(2·G·M/R). For Earth it is about 11.2 km/s.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><defs><marker id='kcek-14' viewBox='0 0 10 10' refX='8' refY='5' markerWidth='5' markerHeight='5' orient='auto-start-reverse'><path d='M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z' fill='var(--c3)'/></marker></defs><circle cx='80' cy='115' r='60' fill='none' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><circle cx='80' cy='115' r='34' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.25' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='80' y='120' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Earth</text><path d='M 80 55 Q 108 57 106.0 93.0' fill='none' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2.5'/><path d='M 80 55 Q 175 50 225 18' fill='none' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2.5' marker-end='url(#kcek-14)'/><circle cx='80' cy='55' r='4' fill='var(--ink)' fill-opacity='1' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='160' y1='96' x2='180' y2='96' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2.5'/><text x='186' y='100' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>low speed: falls back</text><line x1='160' y1='120' x2='180' y2='120' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2.5' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><text x='186' y='124' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>≈ 7.9 km/s: orbit</text><line x1='160' y1='144' x2='180' y2='144' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='2.5'/><text x='186' y='148' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>≥ 11.2 km/s: escapes</text><text x='160' y='192' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>v(escape) = √(2·G·M/R)   (air resistance ignored)</text></svg>
cards.key: Escape velocity does not depend on the object's mass. It is √2 times the orbital speed near the surface (from 7.9 km/s to 11.2 km/s).

cards.h: The energy of a satellite in orbit
cards.p: Gravitational potential energy is Eₚ = −G·M·m/r, and it is zero at infinity. The total energy in orbit is E = −G·M·m/(2r). A satellite that moves lower speeds up, but its total energy decreases.
cards.key: Eₚ is negative because it decreases as the objects get closer, and KE = G·M·m/(2r). In a bound orbit E < 0. Also KE = −E and Eₚ = 2E.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='30' y1='100' x2='300' y2='100' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='24' y='104' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>0</text><rect x='50' y='60' width='60' height='40' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.5' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='80' y='52' font-size='11' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>KE = +GMm/2r</text><rect x='130' y='100' width='60' height='80' fill='var(--c2)' fill-opacity='0.5' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='160' y='195' font-size='11' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>Eₚ = −GMm/r</text><rect x='210' y='100' width='60' height='40' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.5' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='240' y='156' font-size='11' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>E = −GMm/2r</text><text x='310' y='26' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>E = KE + Eₚ < 0</text><text x='310' y='44' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='end'>bound orbit</text></svg>

once.soru: A satellite drops to a lower orbit. What happens to its speed?

secenekler.neden: Since v = √(GM/r), the speed goes up when r gets smaller.
Gravity is stronger lower down. To stay in orbit, the satellite has to move faster.
Orbital speed depends on the radius.

cards.p: The Moon's pull is stronger on the side of Earth facing the Moon and weaker on the far side. This difference creates two bulges of water. That is why the sea rises twice a day on most coasts.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><ellipse cx='145' cy='100' rx='62' ry='45' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.18' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='145' cy='100' r='38' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='145' y='105' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Earth</text><circle cx='285' cy='100' r='12' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.4' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='285' y='130' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Moon</text><text x='78' y='104' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='700'>high tide</text><text x='212' y='92' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' font-weight='700'>high tide</text><text x='145' y='46' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>low tide</text><text x='145' y='163' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>low tide</text><text x='12' y='20' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>the near side is pulled more, the far side less</text><text x='160' y='190' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>most coasts: 2 high + 2 low tides a day (exaggerated)</text></svg>
cards.key: On the near side the water is pulled toward the Moon, and on the far side it is left behind. Tides come from the difference in gravity with distance, not from gravity itself.

once.soru: On most coasts, how many times a day does the sea rise?

secenekler.neden: There is a bulge on each side of Earth. As Earth turns, every coast passes through both.
There is a bulge on the far side too, not only on the side facing the Moon.
There are two bulges. One is on the side facing the Moon, the other on the opposite side.

cards.p:
• The gravitational force is F = G·m₁·m₂/r², and when r doubles F drops to one quarter.
• g = G·M/r². It is about 9.8 m/s² at the surface and 1.6 m/s² on the Moon.
• Kepler's laws: elliptical orbits, equal areas, and T² ∝ r³.
• For a satellite v = √(G·M/r), and weightlessness is free fall.
• Earth's escape velocity is 11.2 km/s.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='10' y='10' width='145' height='85' rx='8' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.12' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='82.5' y='42' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Law of gravitation</text><text x='82.5' y='70' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>F = G·m₁·m₂/r²</text><rect x='165' y='10' width='145' height='85' rx='8' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.12' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='237.5' y='42' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Gravitational accel.</text><text x='237.5' y='70' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>g = G·M/r²</text><rect x='10' y='105' width='145' height='85' rx='8' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.12' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='82.5' y='137' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Kepler 3</text><text x='82.5' y='165' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>T²/r³ = constant</text><rect x='165' y='105' width='145' height='85' rx='8' fill='var(--c5)' fill-opacity='0.12' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='237.5' y='137' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>Orbital speed</text><text x='237.5' y='165' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>v = √(G·M/r)</text></svg>

quiz.q: The gravitational force between two objects is 90 N. If the distance between them is tripled and one of the masses is doubled, what is the new force, in N?
quiz.e: The force is proportional to mass and inversely proportional to the square of the distance. So F' = 90·2/3² = 180/9 = 20 N.

quiz.q: Put the gravitational acceleration g in order from smallest to largest.
ogeler: A height R above Earth's surface (r = 2R)
Height of the space station (≈ 400 km)
quiz.e: On the Moon g is about 1.6 m/s². At r = 2R, g drops to one quarter, about 2.45 m/s². On the space station g is about 8.7 m/s², and at Earth's surface it is about 9.8 m/s².

quiz.q: The orbital radius of a satellite around the same planet is made 4 times larger. How many times longer is its orbital period?
quiz.e: By Kepler's third law, T²/r³ is constant. When r is 4 times larger, T² is 4³ = 64 times larger and T is √64 = 8 times longer.

quiz.q: Two satellites move in circular orbits of the same radius. One has twice the mass of the other. What can you say about their orbital speeds?
o: The heavier one is 2 times faster
The heavier one is √2 times faster
quiz.e: The satellite's mass does not appear in v = √(G·M/r). The speed depends only on the planet's mass and the orbital radius.
y: Orbital speed is v = √(GM/r). The satellite's own mass is not in the formula.
The satellite's mass appears in both the gravitational force and the inertia, so it cancels. There is no √2 difference.
A lighter satellite does not move faster. At the same radius, the speed depends only on the planet's mass.

is-enerji-guc.title: Work, energy, and power
is-enerji-guc.summary: Learn about work, kinetic and potential energy, conservation of energy, and power.

cards.h: Work: when a force moves something
cards.p: When a force moves an object, work is done. Work is W = F·d·cosθ, where θ is the angle between the force and the displacement. Its unit is the joule, and 1 J = 1 N·m.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='20' y1='150' x2='300' y2='150' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><rect x='50' y='110' width='50' height='40' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.5'/><rect x='210' y='110' width='50' height='40' fill='none' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.5' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><line x1='150' y1='110' x2='150' y2='23.4' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-width='1' fill='none' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><line x1='100' y1='110' x2='143' y2='110' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='2' fill='none' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><polygon points='150,110 140,114.5 140,105.5' fill='var(--c1)'/><line x1='100' y1='110' x2='146.5' y2='29.5' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='3' fill='none'/><polygon points='150,23.4 148.9,34.3 141.1,29.8' fill='var(--c1)'/><path d='M125 110 A25 25 0 0 0 112.5 88.3' fill='none' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='127' y='100' font-size='12' fill='var(--acc)'>θ</text><text x='158' y='40' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' font-weight='bold'>F = 50 N</text><text x='155' y='106' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)'>F·cosθ</text><line x1='79.9' y1='170' x2='230.1' y2='170' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='235,170 228,173.2 228,166.8' fill='var(--acc)'/><polygon points='75,170 82,166.8 82,173.2' fill='var(--acc)'/><text x='155' y='190' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>d = 4 m</text><text x='310' y='75' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>W = 100 J</text><text x='310' y='95' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>θ = 60°</text></svg>
cards.key: If a 50 N force acts at a 60° angle over 4 m, then W = 50·4·0.5 = 100 J (cos60° = 0.5).

cards.p: If the force helps the motion, the work is positive. If it opposes the motion (friction), the work is negative. If the force is perpendicular to the motion or the object does not move, the work is zero.

cards.p: A moving object has kinetic energy, given by KE = ½·m·v². The speed enters this formula squared. So when the speed doubles, the energy becomes 4 times larger.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='10' y='18' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)'>1000 kg car</text><line x1='40' y1='170' x2='300' y2='170' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><rect x='60' y='155' width='50' height='15' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.6'/><rect x='140' y='110' width='50' height='60' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.6'/><rect x='220' y='35' width='50' height='135' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.6'/><text x='85' y='148' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>50 kJ</text><text x='165' y='103' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>200 kJ</text><text x='245' y='28' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>450 kJ</text><text x='165' y='145' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>×4</text><text x='245' y='110' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>×9</text><text x='85' y='188' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>10 m/s</text><text x='165' y='188' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>20 m/s</text><text x='245' y='188' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>30 m/s</text></svg>
cards.key: A 1000 kg car moving at 20 m/s has a kinetic energy of ½·1000·20² = 200 000 J.

cards.p: An object lifted higher gains potential energy, given by PE = m·g·h. h is measured from the zero level you choose. A 2 kg book on a 1.5 m shelf has a potential energy of 29.4 J.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='20' y1='180' x2='300' y2='180' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><line x1='262' y1='30' x2='262' y2='180' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='2' fill='none'/><rect x='140' y='60' width='122' height='8' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.5'/><rect x='180' y='36' width='40' height='24' fill='var(--c5)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='var(--c5)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='200' y='53' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>2 kg</text><line x1='110' y1='60' x2='180' y2='60' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-width='1' fill='none' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><line x1='110' y1='173.1' x2='110' y2='66.9' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='110,62 113.2,69 106.8,69' fill='var(--acc)'/><polygon points='110,178 106.8,171 113.2,171' fill='var(--acc)'/><text x='102' y='125' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>h = 1.5 m</text><text x='200' y='25' font-size='13' fill='var(--acc)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>PE = 29.4 J</text><text x='160' y='196' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>zero level (PE = 0)</text></svg>
cards.key: 2·9.8·1.5 = 29.4 J. Here g = 9.8 m/s² was used, but problems often take g = 10.

once.soru: If you put the same book twice as high, what happens to its potential energy?

secenekler.neden: PE = m·g·h. When h doubles, PE doubles too.
The square appears only with speed, in kinetic energy. Potential energy is directly proportional to height.
PE increases as the height increases.

cards.p: The net work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy (Wnet = ΔKE). A cart at rest pushed with a 10 N force over 5 m gains 50 J of kinetic energy.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='15' y1='120' x2='305' y2='120' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><rect x='30' y='90' width='40' height='22' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.5' rx='3'/><circle cx='38' cy='116' r='4' fill='var(--ink)'/><circle cx='62' cy='116' r='4' fill='var(--ink)'/><rect x='230' y='90' width='40' height='22' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.5' rx='3'/><circle cx='238' cy='116' r='4' fill='var(--ink)'/><circle cx='262' cy='116' r='4' fill='var(--ink)'/><line x1='70' y1='101' x2='103' y2='101' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='3' fill='none'/><polygon points='110,101 100,105.5 100,96.5' fill='var(--c1)'/><text x='72' y='84' font-size='12' fill='var(--c1)' font-weight='bold'>F = 10 N</text><text x='28' y='84' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>v = 0</text><line x1='270' y1='101' x2='298' y2='101' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='3' fill='none'/><polygon points='305,101 295,105.5 295,96.5' fill='var(--c3)'/><text x='305' y='84' font-size='12' fill='var(--c3)' text-anchor='end' font-weight='bold'>v ≈ 7.1 m/s</text><line x1='54.9' y1='140' x2='245.1' y2='140' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='250,140 243,143.2 243,136.8' fill='var(--acc)'/><polygon points='50,140 57,136.8 57,143.2' fill='var(--acc)'/><text x='150' y='158' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>d = 5 m</text><text x='50' y='185' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>KE = 0</text><text x='150' y='185' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>W = 10·5 = 50 J</text><text x='255' y='185' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>KE = 50 J</text></svg>
cards.key: The net work is the final kinetic energy minus the initial kinetic energy. With 50 J of energy, a 2 kg cart reaches about 7.1 m/s.

once.soru: A net work of 200 J is done on a car at rest. What is its kinetic energy, in J?

secenekler.neden: The net work equals the change in kinetic energy, and 0 + 200 = 200 J.
Because net work is done, the car speeds up.
All of the net work goes into kinetic energy.

cards.p: As you just saw with the ball, while the potential energy decreases, the kinetic energy increases by the same amount. The sum of KE and PE is called mechanical energy. If only gravity does work, this sum stays constant.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='20' y1='187' x2='100' y2='187' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><line x1='60' y1='37' x2='60' y2='173' stroke='var(--line)' stroke-width='1' fill='none' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><circle cx='60' cy='30' r='7' fill='var(--c1)'/><circle cx='60' cy='105' r='7' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.6'/><circle cx='60' cy='180' r='7' fill='var(--c1)'/><text x='45' y='34' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>5 m</text><text x='45' y='109' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>2.5 m</text><text x='45' y='184' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='end'>0 m</text><text x='110' y='14' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>Total always 98 J</text><rect x='110' y='22' width='120' height='16' fill='var(--c2)' fill-opacity='0.45'/><text x='170' y='34' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>PE = 98 J</text><text x='236' y='34' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>v = 0</text><rect x='110' y='97' width='60' height='16' fill='var(--c2)' fill-opacity='0.45'/><rect x='170' y='97' width='60' height='16' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.45'/><text x='140' y='109' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>PE 49 J</text><text x='200' y='109' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>KE 49 J</text><text x='236' y='109' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>v ≈ 7 m/s</text><rect x='110' y='172' width='120' height='16' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.45'/><text x='170' y='184' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>KE = 98 J</text><text x='236' y='184' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>v ≈ 9.9 m/s</text></svg>
cards.key: KE + PE = constant (if only gravity does work). If work is done from outside (a push), the mechanical energy changes.

etk.soru: Drop the ball from different heights. Does the mass change the impact speed? (No air resistance.)

cards.p: With friction, part of the mechanical energy turns into heat. A child going down a slide slows down, and the slide warms up. The energy turned into heat equals the work done by friction, and the total energy is conserved.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='25' y1='50' x2='150' y2='170' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><line x1='15' y1='170' x2='160' y2='170' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><circle cx='28' cy='40' r='7' fill='var(--c1)'/><circle cx='150' cy='163' r='7' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.6'/><text x='40' y='150' font-size='12' fill='var(--c4)' font-weight='bold'>warms up</text><text x='165' y='40' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>at the start</text><rect x='165' y='48' width='150' height='18' fill='var(--c2)' fill-opacity='0.45'/><text x='240' y='61' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>PE = 100 J</text><text x='240' y='100' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>total still 100 J</text><text x='165' y='125' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>at the end</text><rect x='165' y='133' width='105' height='18' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.45'/><rect x='270' y='133' width='45' height='18' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.55'/><text x='217.5' y='146' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>KE = 70 J</text><text x='292.5' y='168' font-size='12' fill='var(--c4)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>heat 30 J</text></svg>
cards.key: The work done by friction is the initial energy minus the final energy. For a skater who starts with 100 J and ends with 70 J, friction did 30 J of work.

cards.h: The F–x graph and spring energy
cards.p: The area under a force–extension graph gives the work. For a spring F = k·x, so the graph is a triangle. The area of this triangle is the energy stored in the spring, PE = ½·k·x².
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><path d='M40 170 H180 M40 170 V30' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M40 170 L160 50 V170 Z' fill='var(--acc)' fill-opacity='0.2' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='2'/><text x='185' y='184' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='end'>x</text><text x='32' y='36' font-size='12' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='end'>F</text><text x='118' y='150' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>area = work</text><text x='76' y='90' font-size='12' fill='var(--acc)' text-anchor='middle'>F = k·x</text><path d='M210 60 h10 l6 -10 l12 20 l12 -20 l12 20 l12 -20 l6 10 h10' fill='none' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='200' y='40' width='8' height='40' fill='var(--muted)'/><rect x='290' y='48' width='18' height='24' rx='3' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.3' stroke='var(--c1)'/><text x='250' y='105' font-size='14' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>PE = ½·k·x²</text><text x='250' y='128' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>k = 200 N/m, x = 0.1 m</text><text x='250' y='146' font-size='12' fill='var(--acc)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>PE = 1 J</text></svg>
cards.key: If k = 200 N/m and x = 0.1 m, the stored energy is ½·200·0.01 = 1 J.

cards.p: In machines, part of the energy turns into unwanted heat. Efficiency is the useful energy divided by the energy supplied, times 100. Efficiency never exceeds 100%.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='20' y='70' width='80' height='60' rx='8' fill='var(--c4)' fill-opacity='0.15' stroke='var(--c4)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='60' y='96' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>supplied</text><text x='60' y='114' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>100 J</text><path d='M100 100 H150' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='14' stroke-opacity='0.35'/><path d='M150 100 Q200 100 210 60 H240' fill='none' stroke='var(--c3)' stroke-width='6'/><path d='M150 100 Q200 100 210 140 H240' fill='none' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='12' stroke-opacity='0.6'/><text x='246' y='58' font-size='12' fill='var(--c3)' text-anchor='start' font-weight='700'>useful: 20 J</text><text x='246' y='74' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='start'>(light)</text><text x='246' y='140' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)' text-anchor='start' font-weight='700'>lost: 80 J</text><text x='246' y='156' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='start'>(heat)</text><text x='160' y='30' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>efficiency = useful / supplied × 100</text><text x='120' y='186' font-size='12' fill='var(--acc)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='700'>bulb efficiency: 20%</text></svg>

once.soru: A bulb turns 20 J of every 100 J of electrical energy into light. What is its efficiency, in percent?

secenekler.neden: The ratio of useful energy to supplied energy is 20 / 100 = 0.2, which is 20%.
80% is the part that goes into heat, not the useful part.
Efficiency cannot exceed 100%.

cards.h: Power: how fast work is done
cards.p: Power is the work done per unit time, P = W / t. Its unit is the watt, and 1 W = 1 J/s. A person who runs up the stairs uses more power than one who walks up.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M20 170 h20 v-20 h20 v-20 h20 v-20 h20 v-20 h20 v-20 h20 v-20 h30 V170 Z' fill='var(--panel)' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='20' y='30' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>W = 1470 J (both)</text><line x1='180' y1='165.1' x2='180' y2='54.9' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='180,50 183.2,57 176.8,57' fill='var(--acc)'/><polygon points='180,170 176.8,163 183.2,163' fill='var(--acc)'/><text x='186' y='114' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>3 m</text><line x1='205' y1='170' x2='312' y2='170' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><rect x='212' y='52.4' width='45' height='117.6' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.5'/><rect x='264' y='111.2' width='45' height='58.8' fill='var(--c3)' fill-opacity='0.5'/><text x='234.5' y='46' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>294 W</text><text x='286.5' y='105' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>147 W</text><text x='234.5' y='160' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>running</text><text x='286.5' y='160' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>walking</text><text x='234.5' y='188' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>5 s</text><text x='286.5' y='188' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>10 s</text></svg>
cards.key: A 50 kg person who climbs 3 m does about 1470 J of work. Doing it in 5 s takes 294 W, and in 10 s it takes 147 W. 1 kWh is 3.6 million J.

cards.p: If an object moves at a constant speed v under a force F, the power is P = F·v. If you push a crate with a 500 N force at a constant 2 m/s, the power is 1000 W.
cards.key: P = W/t = F·d/t = F·v. That is why you shift to a low gear on a hill. It gives you a large force at a low speed.
cards.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='20' y='30' font-size='13' fill='var(--ink)' font-weight='bold'>P = F·v = 500·2 = 1000 W</text><line x1='10' y1='140' x2='310' y2='140' stroke='var(--ink)' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><rect x='130' y='90' width='70' height='50' fill='var(--c1)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='var(--c1)' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='165' y='120' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)' text-anchor='middle'>crate</text><line x1='50' y1='115' x2='122' y2='115' stroke='var(--acc)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='130,115 121,110.5 121,119.5' fill='var(--acc)'/><text x='86' y='106' font-size='12' fill='var(--acc)' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='bold'>F = 500 N</text><line x1='190' y1='150' x2='138' y2='150' stroke='var(--c2)' stroke-width='2.5' fill='none'/><polygon points='130,150 139,145.5 139,154.5' fill='var(--c2)'/><text x='196' y='155' font-size='12' fill='var(--c2)'>friction 500 N</text><line x1='140' y1='72' x2='182' y2='72' stroke='var(--muted)' stroke-width='2' fill='none'/><polygon points='190,72 181,67.5 181,76.5' fill='var(--muted)'/><text x='198' y='76' font-size='12' fill='var(--ink)'>v = 2 m/s (constant)</text><text x='160' y='186' font-size='11' fill='var(--muted)' text-anchor='middle'>net force zero, yet the push does 1000 J each second</text></svg>

once.soru: A car with constant engine power starts up a hill and needs a larger force. What happens to its speed?

secenekler.neden: If P = F·v is constant, v gets smaller when F gets larger.
With constant power, the speed cannot increase when the force increases.
The product F·v is constant. So when F changes, v changes too.

cards.p: Energy comes in many forms. Kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, electrical, light, sound, and nuclear energy are some of them. All are measured in joules and can turn into one another. The total energy is conserved.

once.soru: In what order does the water's energy change at a dam?

secenekler.neden: The water falls from a height and speeds up, it turns the turbine, and the generator produces electricity.
That is a thermal power plant. No fuel burns at a dam.
That is a nuclear power plant.

cards.p:
Work is W = F·d·cosθ, and its unit is the joule.
KE = ½mv² and PE = mgh. The net work equals the change in kinetic energy.
If only gravity does work, KE + PE stays constant. Friction turns energy into heat.
Power is P = W/t = F·v.
For a spring PE = ½kx². Efficiency is the ratio of useful energy to supplied energy.
